Commentary.Commentary: Time for the trophy lift - Tom Latham collects the winners' trophy and joins his teammates in posing for a team photo. Not many surprises in this one-off Test, and even a fairly inexperienced New Zealand side proved to be very overpowering against an Irish side that was dealing with a few player transitions as well. Overall, this will give plenty of exposure to the young players on both sides as they navigate their way through red-ball cricket. Moving on, New Zealand now set their eyes on the Crowe-Thorpe Trophy as they travel to England for a three-match Test series beginning on June 4. The first Test of the series will be played at Lord's and will begin at 10 am GMT, so be sure to join us for that. As for Ireland, they have a bit of a break before welcoming India for a white-ball series late in June. We bid adieu for now and hope you enjoyed our coverage. Until next time, then, take care, and goodbye!

The captain of New Zealand - Tom Latham says that they put good pressure on the Irish batting side, and it worked well. He adds that Nathan Smith was brilliant with the ball and Blair Tickner was relentless in the last innings as well. He reckons that it was a nice test and they will hope to come back here and play again. He reckons that they were put under pressure with the new ball, but they made a good comeback and put the pressure back on the opponents. He says that Rachin and Blundell had a great partnership, and there were other players who stepped up as well. He ends by saying that they are happy to come and play here in Belfast, and they are happy to play this Test match.

Let's now hear from the skipper of Ireland - Andy Balbirnie starts by speaking on the performance of their opposition. He says that they were phenomenal with their cricket. Adds that they were clinical with their bowling performances and have played really well throughout the three days. Continues that his team started really well in the first inning, as their bowlers got the rhythm, but as the game rolled on, the Kiwis got hold of the game. On his toss decision to bowl first, he says that he wouldn't change that decision even with the reult in mind. Balbirnie further adds that they needed to execute their plans better. As he said earlier, they started very well but failed to continue with the momentum. On the performances of their three debutants, he says that they played very well. They have huge talent, but it needs guidance to get better results. About the future of Irish cricket, the skipper comments that they want to play more Test cricket, as the boys love to play this long format of cricket. Ends up congratulating the Kiwis for winning the match.

POTM - Tom Blundell is the Player of the Match for his excellent knock of 186 runs. He says that it feels good, and it was good to get support from Rachin Ravindra as well. He further says that the wicket was a bit difficult to bat on. He reckons that their bowlers did a great job with the ball, and Dean Foxcroft had a brilliant debut as well with the bat. He ends by saying that he has enjoyed his time here, and the weather was great as well. They are well prepared for the England tour.
The Presentation ceremony...

Let's recap the first two days - After putting New Zealand into bat and fielding as many as three debutants, Ireland made early inroads and even managed to bog down the visitors to 86/4. However, things shifted drastically after that and the Irish bowlers found it really difficult to get a breakthrough. Rachin Ravindra and Tom Blundell put on a staggering stand of 217 runs, and both of them notched up their tons as well. Blundell then put on 158 runs with Dean Foxcroft as well before falling for 186. Foxcroft, playing his maiden Test match agonizingly short of a debut ton as he got out on 98 and the Kiwis declared at 490/8. Ireland were under the pump and were 38/6, staring at a lead in excess of 400 runs in the first innings. That's when Andy McBrine and Mark Adair stitched together a 116-run stand and the hosts eventually got bowled out for 179 runs. Nathan Smith was the wrecker-in-chief, picking up 6 wickets as the Kiwis enforced the follow-on, whilst having a first innings lead of 311 runs. Day 2 ended with Ireland 65/2 in their second innings with Blair Tickner doing the early damage.

A short Test to say the least - It was a shortened four-day Test, but New Zealand only required a couple of days and a couple of sessions on Day 3 to seal the win. Ireland began the day at 65/2, but the first session belonged to the visitors as they picked up a few wickets and until late in the session, there were hardly any runs scored. Things changed in the second session as Ireland started to go after the bowling a bit, with the likes of Stephen Doheny and Lorcan Tucker scoring a couple of half-centuries. Mark Adair scored an unbeaten 44 to drag down the margin of defeat by a fair bit, but it was still a hefty loss. Blair Tickner was the pick of the bowlers in the second innings, as he picked up a maiden Test five-fer, making good use of the short ball more often than not.

New Zealand reign supreme - The Kiwis flex their Test-match experience and hand Ireland a thumping, as they win by an innings and 79 runs. Also, with Curtis Campher unable to bat due to an injury, Ireland's second innings comes to an end with 9 wickets lost.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 3. The on-air commentators inform us that Curtis Campher is probably at a hospital, getting scans done on his left hand. The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of New Zealand. Andy McBrine and Lorcan Tucker will resume their stay at the crease, and Zakary Foulkes will complete his unfinished over. Let's go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Live to fight another day? With plenty of time still left on Day 3, the big question is whether Ireland can bat for a couple of more sessions and take the game into the final day or not. The scoring rate has picked up significantly in the last few overs and Tucker seems to be playing a solid knock. However, the Kiwis will know that a wicket or two here and they will have the opportunity to go for the kill. Do join us for what should be a fascinating post-Lunch session beginning at 1 pm GMT.

Ireland looking to dig deep - Coming into the day at 65/2, Ireland needed some resistance and that's what Stephen Doheny gave them. However, Nathan Smith bowled a top spell from one end and Blair Tickner got the ball to bounce up and down a lot and both bowlers picked up a wicket each in their opening spells to put the hosts into a spot of bother. Doheny did reach his maiden Test half-century, but couldn't kick on, and Curtis Campher was retired hurt, adding to Ireland's woes as Tickner picked up a four-fer.

The Kiwis strengthen their grip - Right then, the first session on Day 3 has been cut short by 10-12 minutes, but we have witnessed plenty of action. For now, New Zealand still lead by 180 big runs, and they need 5 more wickets to wrap up the Test. However, Ireland have their top two all-time leading scorers in Tests in the form of Andy McBrine and Lorcan Tucker, and will hope that they put on a big stand. Also, the squabble lasted just a couple of minutes and it is now all clear once again.

Uh, oh! The few drops of rain have quickly turned into a drizzle. The umpires call for covers and the players are going off. The Irish batters certainly won't mind an early Lunch break. And, it is official now, as the umpires have called for LUNCH ON DAY 3.

A word with the debutant, Reuben Wilson - Reuben Wilson says that it's been a tough time for them so far, but they have given their best. He adds that they have enjoyed their couple of days of cricket. He further says that he was happy with his first wicket and ends by saying that he didn't get off the mark with the bat in the first innings, but if he gets a chance to bat in the second innings, he will score some runs as well.

A quick chat with Dean Foxcroft - Dean Foxcroft says that he is a bit disappointed to be dismissed on 98, but they are in a good position to win this game. Adds that he just got a top edge as he was trying to get his hundred. He reckons that they bowled pretty well and they are in a strong position, and ends by saying that hopefully they will strike early and win this game.

PITCH REPORT - Katey Martin says that it is overcast and windy, which will aid the bowlers. On the deck, she says that there are still cracks in the wicket, which will continue to dry out, but there aren't many demons in it. She further adds that someone like Rachin Ravindra will come into play, and the spinners might get a bit of drift as well. Overall, she says that there is an opportunity for an Irish batter to score big as well.

The plan for today? The scripts for both dressing rooms are completely different this morning. For New Zealand, the mission is simple. Attack from ball one, extract any morning moisture left in the surface, and wrap up a clinical victory before the day ends. For Ireland, it is entirely about survival. They need to block out the noise, eat up time, erase this massive deficit, and force New Zealand to bat again. Can they do it? We shall find out...

The equation right now - Forced to bat a second time, Ireland have started with a much cooler head, currently sitting at 65/2 after 16 overs. Blair Tickner broke an encouraging 42-run opening stand by picking up skipper Andrew Balbirnie and Cade Carmichael in quick succession. Stephen Doheny has looked good and he is out there right now alongside the nightwatchman. As it stands, Ireland still trail by 246 runs with 8 wickets left in the bag.

So, how did the Kiwis take control? Yesterday was a masterclass in modern Test cricket by the Kiwis. Resuming at 361/5, New Zealand powered their way to a mammoth 490/8 and declared. Tom Blundell was the star of the show, hammering a career-best 186 alongside Rachin Ravindra’s spectacular 121. Spare a thought for debutant Dean Foxcroft, who was agonizingly dismissed just two runs short of a dream century on 98. When Ireland came out to bat, Kiwi speedster Nathan Smith absolutely tore through the top order, picking up an incredible fifer to leave the hosts reeling at 38/6. A brilliant 116-run counter-attacking partnership between Andy McBrine and Mark Adair gave Ireland some respectability, pulling them up to 179, but it wasn't enough to avoid the follow-on.

Welcome to Day 3 at Stormont - A very warm welcome back to our live coverage of this historic one-off Test match. The weather is set and we are tuning in for a game that could very well be the final day of this match. New Zealand enters the day firmly in the driver’s seat, while Ireland faces a massive mountain to climb if they want to survive the spin and swing today.

Day 2 concludes - That wraps up all the action from Day 2. It was another day that completely belonged to the visiting team, leaving New Zealand miles ahead in this Test match. Ireland now faces a massive challenge. The home team must first clear the remaining 246-run deficit before they can build a target to fight against the Kiwis. The exciting battle will resume on Day 3 on May 29, 2026, at 10 am GMT. Cheers!

Word from the Irish camp - Andy McBrine is up for a chat. Andy says that he is happy with his individual performance with the bat. On the partnership between him and Adair, he says that he enjoyed batting with Mark, and also adds that when he was batting, he just wanted to add more and more runs on the board. However, he would have liked it if they pushed their scoreboard more. Andy adds that they have a huge task tomorrow, and they will try to bat deep into the day.

NZ's star with the ball, Nathan Smith - Nathan Smith says that he enjoyed the condition as the ball was moving well off the deck. Nathan adds that it's a bit hard to bowl with the old ball, but he is happy with the way they have been playing. On his first five-fer, he comments that he feels great to contribute something to the team and it always feels good to have wickets under the column. Nathan Smith credits Dean Foxcroft, saying that it was wonderful to watch him play and also notes that it's the partnership between Dean Foxcroft and Rachin Ravindran that revived the batting innings for them.

Ireland fights hard after follow-on - Since Ireland was behind by 311 runs, New Zealand made them bat again straight away. The Irish openers did a much better job in their second turn. They put on 42 runs for the first wicket before captain Andy Balbirnie edged a ball from Blair Tickner to wicketkeeper Tom Blundell. Cade Carmichael walked out, replacing his skipper, but got a beauty from Blair and had to make the long walks as well. Ireland ended Day 2 at 65 for 2 and still trail by 246 runs. Doheny looked much more confident and sits on 36 not out, while the nightwatchman, Thomas Mayes, has done what he was sent out to do and is unbeaten on 4 heading into Day 3.

Fightback and a brilliant spell from Smith - Just when it looked like Ireland would be bowled out quickly, Mark Adair and Andy McBrine saved the day with a brave 116-run partnership. They lifted the team from 38 for 6 to 154 before Nathan Smith finally dismissed Adair. The rest of the batting order fell fast, and Ireland was bowled out for 179 runs. Nathan Smith was the star bowler for New Zealand, taking an amazing 6 wickets to claim his first-ever five-wicket haul. Ben Sears took two wickets in the same over to clean up the tail, while Zakary Foulkes and Blair Tickner got one wicket each.

Ireland's top order crumbles before Lunch - Ireland had a terrible start to their first innings against New Zealand's big total. The Kiwi bowlers put heavy pressure on the home team right away. Ireland lost two quick wickets in just six overs while scoring only 20 runs before the Lunch break. Things got even worse in the afternoon session as the New Zealand bowlers took total control. Ireland lost four more wickets quickly, leaving them in deep trouble at 38 for 6.

Kiwis power ahead and declare on Day 2 - New Zealand started the day at 361 for 5 and batted very well in the morning. Tom Blundell and Dean Foxcroft built a strong 158-run partnership to push the team total to 461. Blundell eventually got out after scoring a brilliant 186 runs. Foxcroft kept fighting alongside Nathan Smith and Zakary Foulkes but got out just two runs short of a century on his Test debut. As soon as Foxcroft fell, New Zealand declared their first innings at a massive 490 for 8.

STUMPS ON DAY 2 - New Zealand have totally dominated Day 2 of the Test match. They started by adding quick runs to their score in the morning. Then, the bowlers took over and grabbed 12 wickets on the same day. Ireland were bowled out for just 179 runs in their first innings. Since they trailed by 311 runs, New Zealand forced them to bat again straight away by enforcing the follow-on. The visitors are now miles ahead in this contest.
